clue.text: Essay about object that's fashionable

indicators.note: one word placed about another wraps around it, so the essay goes outside the object

blocks.note: an essay is an attempt
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: A student hands in a composition on some fashionable topic.
explanation.walkthrough: Object here is a goal, not a thing: 'to what end?' asks the object.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trendy follows the latest styles, matching current popular taste.

clue.text: Bill allows some medicine

blocks.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab
lets means permits

explanation.surface: Somebody named Bill gives permission for a little medication.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name; it is the bar bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Tablets are pills, small pressed doses in which medicine is commonly taken.

clue.text: England's first team takes both ends outdoors

indicators.note: the first of England is its opening letter
both ends of a word are its opening and closing letters only

blocks.note: the opening letter of England
a cricket or football team has eleven players, written in Roman numerals
the outside letters of takes

explanation.surface: England's top side picks up two goals at either end of an open-air pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Read outdoors as 'out doors': doors leading out.
explanation.definitionFit: Exits are the doors by which people go out of a building, hence 'out doors'.

clue.text: Self-indulgent life of fool upset by musical

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the word for fool reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a clod is a dull, stupid person
Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Peron

explanation.surface: A buffoon is put out by a stage show, while living a pampered life.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase means 'the sweet life', a byword for luxurious, pleasure-seeking idleness.

clue.text: Capital containing a hospital for outcasts

indicators.note: the capital city holds the other letters inside it

blocks.note: the capital of France
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A capital city with a hospital set aside for social rejects.
explanation.definitionFit: Pariahs are people shunned and excluded by society, just as outcasts are.

clue.text: Crushing remark that's recorded

blocks.note: first meaning: a humiliating snub
second meaning: written down, entered in writing

explanation.surface: A devastating insult that has been preserved on tape.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the phrase is a deflating snub; as a verb phrase it means noted in writing.

clue.text: After religious instruction heaven appears unsafe

blocks.note: RI is the school abbreviation for religious instruction
the sky, the heavens

explanation.surface: After a scripture lesson, the afterlife suddenly seems dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: After places the scripture letters first, before the word for heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Risky means involving danger or hazard, so not safe.

clue.text: Purple and gold mixture of beer and gin

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the letters of the drinks are jumbled

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the letters of beer and gin, rearranged

explanation.surface: A cocktail of beer and gin turns out purple and gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' after Purple joins definition to wordplay; 'and' in 'beer and gin' is not fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergine is a dark purple shade, named after the skin of the eggplant.

clue.text: Look round shelter, being ready for bed

indicators.note: the word for look goes round the shelter, enclosing it

blocks.note: to spy is to look
the lee is the sheltered side, out of the wind

explanation.surface: Someone peers around a refuge, tired and ready to turn in.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepy person is drowsy and tired, wanting to go to sleep.

clue.text: Religious teacher with time for timid person

blocks.note: a rabbi is a Jewish teacher of the law
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A clergyman with time to spare for a nervous pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit is British slang for a feeble or cowardly person, especially a poor sports player.

clue.text: Very clever fish ain't at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: brill is a flatfish
the letters of ain't, rearranged

explanation.surface: A gifted fish is out of the water, oddly, although the phrase would suggest it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant describes someone exceptionally intelligent or talented.

clue.text: Island's turning black

indicators.note: turning round means the island's name is read back to front

blocks.note: Elba, Napoleon's island of exile, with the 's

explanation.surface: An island going dark as night falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic and poetic word for the colour black.

clue.text: Follow headless queens around

indicators.note: without a head means the opening letter is lost
going around moves letters from the front to the back in a loop

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Coming after decapitated royals, perhaps in a Tudor history.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the Q, then move the first two letters UE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after or result, as one event follows another.

clue.text: Show disapproval by     taking carriage as a sort of practical joke

blocks.note: to boo is to jeer
taken as written
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse carriage

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at being given a ride in a coach as a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby trap is a hidden device or prank set to catch out an unsuspecting victim.

clue.text: So deep in thought one's absorbed - nobody will play with one

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken right inside, so the word for one sits within the word for deep in thought

blocks.note: taken as written
lost in thought, absorbed in thinking
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone so wrapped up in their own thoughts that no one will join their game.
explanation.walkthrough: One's here is 'one is', and absorbed works twice: the thinker is absorbed, and one is absorbed into the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A soloist performs alone, with no other musician accompanying the part.

clue.text: Prescribed bedtime in lands abroad

blocks.note: a bird lights, or alights, when it lands
abroad means out and about, outside

explanation.surface: Going to bed at an official time while travelling in foreign countries.
explanation.walkthrough: Lands looks like a noun for countries; it is a verb, coming down to land.
explanation.definitionFit: In schools, barracks and camps, the set time when lamps go off and everyone must sleep.

clue.text: A drink with a head

blocks.note: first meaning: a small measure of liquor
second meaning: informal word for the skull or brain

explanation.surface: A beer with a good frothy top on it.
explanation.walkthrough: A head on a drink is froth, but here it is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a small cup or quarter-pint of spirits and, colloquially, a person's skull.

clue.text: Latin verbal adjective given rude translation

indicators.note: translating turns words into a different form, so these letters are rendered in a new order

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A schoolboy renders a Latin grammar term with a smutty version.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin grammar this form, like 'Agenda', is an adjective made from a verb expressing obligation.

clue.text: Appalled - but helping to make Branagh a star

indicators.note: the letters needed only help make up the phrase, forming a part of it

blocks.note: found inside the run of letters across the words

explanation.surface: Someone horrified at the idea of promoting Kenneth Branagh to fame.
explanation.walkthrough: Kenneth Branagh is a British actor and director.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or shock, just as being appalled is.

clue.text: Kitchen order: stir in flour, possibly

indicators.note: putting into order rearranges, so the letters of the room are set out afresh

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: An instruction given in the kitchen: add flour while stirring.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchen order reads like a cook's command, but order is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring in flour is one way a cook makes a sauce or gravy denser, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Present course

blocks.note: first meaning: belonging to now, of today
second meaning: a flow, as of a river or of electricity

explanation.surface: A gift of a series of lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for what exists now and a noun for a moving stream of water or air.

clue.text: Clergymen preserve son, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints at a looser version, so the letters of son are rearranged

blocks.note: to can food is to preserve it
the letters of son, rearranged

explanation.surface: Priests try to protect a boy, maybe their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Canons are clergy attached to a cathedral, members of its chapter.

clue.text: Cry in the field though little colleague is content

indicators.note: being the content of something means sitting inside it, filling it

blocks.note: tho is the shortened spelling of though
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: A shout outdoors while a junior co-worker is happy.
explanation.walkthrough: Little tells you to shorten the word before it. Content looks like 'happy'; it means contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Huntsmen shout it in the hunting field on sighting the fox.

clue.text: Spanish-speaking area of city - except for a Portuguese-speaking city

blocks.note: bar means except, as in 'all bar one'
Rio de Janeiro in Brazil

explanation.surface: A Spanish quarter of a town, unlike a city where Portuguese is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrio is a district or quarter of a city in Spain or Spanish-speaking America.

clue.text: Two chaps like some medieval legends

blocks.note: two men's names, Arthur and Ian

explanation.surface: A pair of men who resemble old tales of chivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: The two names are ARTHUR and IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The tales of King Arthur, the Round Table and Camelot are a body of medieval romances.

clue.text: Sort of blume? Sort of bloom?

indicators.note: a sort of version suggests a rough reworking, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: a nonsense word, there just for its letters

explanation.surface: A puzzled gardener asks whether a misspelt flower name is some kind of blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: The same two words do different jobs: first they signal a rearrangement, then they define. The misspelt blume echoes bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbel is a flower cluster whose stalks spread from one point, as in cow parsley.

clue.text: Philanthropist retiring for the good of France

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the French words are read backwards

blocks.note: le bon is French for the good

explanation.surface: A shy benefactor working for the benefit of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel left his fortune to endow the prizes bearing his name.

clue.text: Container containing a small container

indicators.note: one word holds the others inside it

blocks.note: a bin is a receptacle
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: One receptacle nested inside another, like Russian dolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is a bowl for holding water or food, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Letter from Greek graduate - it has four sides

blocks.note: rho is the Greek letter R
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a degree

explanation.surface: A correspondence sent by a Greek alumnus on a square-shaped page.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb, or rhombus, is a parallelogram whose sides are all equal: a quadrilateral.

clue.text: King accompanied by aerial artist

blocks.note: K is king in chess notation
and means together with
aerial means up in the air, in the sky

explanation.surface: A monarch goes about with a painter who flies.
explanation.walkthrough: Aerial looks like a TV antenna; it is the adjective meaning airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassily Kandinsky was a Russian painter, a pioneer of abstract art.

clue.text: Bird discovered by dramatist outside Los Angeles

indicators.note: one name lies outside the other, surrounding it

blocks.note: Joe Orton, the English playwright of Loot
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A playwright spots a bird just beyond the city limits of Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European bunting, once eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Nothing on listed building?

blocks.note: a ship lists, or leans, to one side
the circle of zero

explanation.surface: An empty protected building, perhaps one listed as historic.
explanation.walkthrough: On places the nothing after the word for listed. In Britain a listed building is one protected for its historic value.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed or extension whose roof rests against a larger wall, a simple structure.
